anomalies.description: A bright flash and rapidly expanding light source appears near the center-left of the frame around 16.5s–17.5s, consistent with ignition of a fire or explosive device. A person is visible nearby (near the parked van) just before and during the onset, moving away quickly after the flash—suggesting deliberate fire-setting. The light intensifies and spreads across the ground, indicating a growing fire. No vehicle collision or natural cause (e.g., electrical fault) is evident; the suddenness and localized origin point to arson.

A small fire or intense light source appears abruptly on the ground near a vehicle at ~18.0s and grows progressively over time (visible smoke and expanding glow through frames), consistent with deliberate ignition (arson). A person is briefly visible near the origin point in early frames before moving away, supporting suspicion of intentional fire-setting.

A bright, rapidly intensifying light source appears on the left side of the frame (likely ground-level), accompanied by increasing smoke/dust plume—consistent with a small fire igniting and growing over time. No visible person is clearly present at the origin point in these frames, but the sudden emergence and expansion of the light/smoke without an obvious accidental cause (e.g., vehicle collision or electrical fault) strongly suggests deliberate ignition (arson). The fire grows progressively across frames 1–12, matching the expected pattern of a small fire starting from one point and expanding.
